title: Is Oracle Stock a Buying Opportunity Right Now?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; the DCF fair value figure and the exact PEG digits were not captured in the captions (numbers dropped in auto-captions), so no fair value is recorded.
summary: Parkevtate asks whether Oracle's 44% year-to-date fall in 2026 is a buying opportunity. The business is booming: remaining performance obligations grew $26bn in a single quarter, mostly prepay or bring-your-own-hardware contracts that need no incremental Oracle investment, and analysts expect earnings per share to grow 30% a year. But the stock is being sold because free cash flow is negative ($23bn of operating cash flow against $28bn of capex), long-term debt has reached $165bn against over $37bn of cash, fiscal 2027 capex is planned at $90-95bn, and funding the backlog may mean more equity raises and dilution - Oracle has already done a $20bn equity sale. Borrowing costs have risen a couple of hundred basis points in three months, and he cites SpaceX paying nearly 10% on recent debt. Valuation is the cheapest it has ever been on his measures: forward PE about 10x and a PEG of about 0.3x, with operating margins averaging about 34% over the past decade. Call: ORCL BUY, first explicit call (prior mention UNCERTAIN on 19 Oct), medium conviction - 'risk versus reward is excellent for Oracle stock investors in the long run'. Base case: the backlog converts and free cash flow turns positive in the second half of fiscal 2028, reaching $30bn-plus in fiscal 2029. Bear case: rising borrowing costs force dilutive raises, with heavy OpenAI concentration in the backlog. Similar models CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius are mentioned.
